name: FICTIONAL rehearsal: unstabilised approach, long landing and runway excursion
note: Invented to rehearse the EASA slot. Not a real occurrence; every fact below is made up.

fdm_rules.name: ground speed > VREF + 20 kt below 1000 ft
above the glide path by > 1 dot (~0.35 deg) below 1000 ft

events.text: cleared ILS RWY 26, maintain 180 kt to 4 NM
wind 080/10 kt (tailwind on RWY 26), runway wet
PF: 'we will make it'; no go-around call

Decision errors: continued an approach unstable at 1000 ft and 500 ft
Crew resource management: PM did not call 'go around' at the stabilisation gate
Adverse mental states: plan continuation bias under schedule pressure
Physical environment: tailwind and wet runway reduced the stopping margin
Inadequate supervision: FDM had flagged unstable approaches on this route without follow-up
Organisational climate: on-time performance targets emphasised in crew briefings

ercs.severity_reason: assessed: a ~60 kt overrun into the runway end area makes a hull loss with 20-100 fatalities the credible worst outcome, not the loss of all 143 on board (judgement)

safety_recommendations.text: add a mandatory 'stable / go around' call at 1000 ft and 500 ft with no-fault go-around policy; audit compliance through FDM within 6 months
close the loop on FDM unstable-approach events: crew debrief within 14 days and route-level trend review each quarter
assess a runway end safety area or arresting system for RWY 26 within 12 months
evaluate certification of on-board runway overrun awareness and alerting for new large aeroplanes (systemic; SRUR candidate)
